analysis: What changed vs the 4:00 AM brief: futures firmed slightly (S&P E-mini +0.13% at 05:03 ET, with later snapshots up to +0.25%), Nvidia's bounce extended to about +2% premarket, and the Microsoft drag deepened — MSFT is now -2.6% premarket vs -1.53% an hour ago as the outage entered day two with only 'marginal success'. The new overnight mover is Modine: Bloomberg reports Samsung is in talks to acquire the data-center cooling maker, and the stock is +23-31% premarket on a report neither company has confirmed. Oil's Thursday jump is now fully sourced — Brent $95.82 (+3.3%), WTI $88.74 (+2.6%) — but it rests on Houthi claims with no Saudi confirmation of damage, so the premium is fragile. Washington entered the Nvidia story: Huang agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving and Trump publicly backed Tim Cook as CEO, while Reuters reported a relationship with a third Nvidia employee that neither Huang nor the company has confirmed. Cisco's fade also deepened to about -3.0% premarket. Signal vs noise: PPI at 8:30 AM ET, the outage's slow fix, and the Modine report are the live wires; the Cook endorsement is theater (the board decides), and the oil premium and Modine premium both sit on unverified claims. The tape's real headwind is unchanged: the 10-year at 5.12% with a December hike fully priced.

community_signals.takeaway: 358 comments shifting from the resignation itself to what the board knew, who could succeed Huang, and whether the ~$1.6T drawdown since early October had already priced governance risk — adds succession-speculation color beyond the headlines.
community_signals.title: Former Nvidia CEO Huang had a relationship with a second employee, sources say

disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving, House Foreign Affairs chair Mast said, and President Trump publicly backed Apple's Tim Cook to replace him as CEO. NVDA is +~2% premarket, holding above Thursday's $148.80 intraday low after closing at $166.19 (-4.34%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The testimony agreement and a high-profile succession endorsement move the story from the boardroom to Washington, but the permanent-CEO question is still open — the bounce is relief, not resolution. Note: a Reuters report of a relationship with a third Nvidia employee is unconfirmed by Huang and the company.

headlines.headline: Microsoft's 365 outage is into day two with only 'marginal success' so far: Microsoft says a process on affected servers that establishes secure connections becomes overwhelmed, and it is validating a configuration change before a wider rollout. MSFT is -2.6% premarket per Reuters, deeper than -1.53% at 4 AM; the outage hit users in 74 countries and delayed Richemont's results and Japan's finance ministry email.
headlines.why_it_matters: A second day with no confirmed root cause, and a second major outage in a month, turns this into a reliability and concentration story for Microsoft's cloud — the drag on the stock is widening, not fading.

headlines.headline: Bloomberg reports Samsung is in talks to acquire data-center cooling maker Modine, with a deal possibly coming together in weeks. Modine is +23-31% premarket (about $131 vs Thursday's $106.10 close, after touching $137.45 after hours); no price has been disclosed, no decision made, and neither company has confirmed anything.
headlines.why_it_matters: A reported bid for the cooling layer of the AI buildout is a sentiment tailwind for AI infrastructure names — but with no price and talks that could still collapse, the premium is fragile. Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile.

headlines.headline: Cerebras is +17-19% premarket after its Q3 beat and raised 2026 outlook, with market-mover roundups newly reporting Microsoft as a cloud customer.
headlines.why_it_matters: A Microsoft customer win would validate Cerebras as a real second source in AI compute — but the customer detail comes from market-mover roundups, not a company release, so treat it as unconfirmed until Cerebras or Microsoft says it.

headlines.headline: Brent settled at $95.82 (+3.3%) and WTI at $88.74 (+2.6%) on Thursday after Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on three Saudi energy sites and Iran's military said four tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz. The Houthis did not say when the attacks took place and there was no Saudi confirmation of damage; Reuters could not verify the tanker claim.
headlines.why_it_matters: Oil's jump is priced on unverified claims, so the premium can unwind fast if no damage is confirmed — but with the IEA's monthly oil report due today, energy stays a live tape driver.

headlines.headline: Futures are mixed into the open: S&P E-mini +0.13% and Dow +0.06% at 05:03 ET, Nasdaq 100 -0.11%, with the VIX easing to 18.20. Europe's Stoxx 600 opened -0.26% and Asian shares were mostly lower with modest losses as investors weigh the Nvidia fallout. October PPI prints at 8:30 AM ET (expected +0.4% MoM).
headlines.why_it_matters: A flat-to-mixed tape with the 10-year at 5.12% and the 2-year at 4.88% means PPI is the tiebreaker — a hot print would likely hit the rate-sensitive names that led Thursday's slide.

headlines.headline: Flowers Foods is -12.6% premarket after a Q3 miss and an outlook cut.
headlines.why_it_matters: A staples name cutting its outlook is a small sentiment drag and a reminder that this earnings season's misses are still being punished.
